solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Wood by motorway provides food for animals

parts.note: M is the standard abbreviation for a motorway, as in the M1
ash is a tree and the timber it gives

explanation.surface: Timber stacked beside a motorway ends up as fodder for livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: Mash is a mixture of boiled grain or bran fed to horses and other livestock.

clue.text: Chap almost challenging high-ranking bureaucrat

parts.note: a chap is a man

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the synonym is left off

parts.note: a daring feat is a challenging one

explanation.surface: A fellow who is nearly defiant takes on a senior official.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts the G from DARING, leaving DARIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandarin was a senior official of imperial China, now any powerful civil servant.

clue.text: Plant fake diamond

parts.note: a sham is a fake
rock is slang for a diamond

explanation.surface: Someone plants a counterfeit gem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' reads as a verb (to plant a fake diamond on someone) but is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The shamrock is a clover-like plant, the emblem of Ireland.

clue.text: Fern, perhaps, up the salon for new styling

indicators.note: styling something anew rearranges it, so these letters are restyled into a new order

explanation.surface: A hairdresser is told to brighten up the salon with a fern.
explanation.definitionFit: A fern is one example of a plant grown indoors in a pot.

clue.text: Painting style round area

parts.note: O is round in shape
a part, as in 'these parts', is an area or region

explanation.surface: An artistic style is said to surround a region.
explanation.walkthrough: OP ART is short for optical art, the 1960s abstract style built on visual illusions.
explanation.definitionFit: Op art is an abstract art movement using patterns that seem to move.

clue.text: One watching a game could make a protest about clubs

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the other piece
says the letters of the following words could be made into something else

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs, the card suit

explanation.surface: A fan at a match might complain about the football clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could make' rearranges A PROTEST into SPETATOR, and 'about' puts it around C.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectator is someone who watches an event, such as a sports match, without taking part.

clue.text: Strange formality in gym gets to delay things

indicators.note: in puts the jumbled letters inside the other piece

parts.note: PE, physical education, is school gym

indicators.note: something strange is out of its normal order, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: An odd bit of ceremony in the gym holds everything up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strange' turns FORMALITY into LAYFORTIM, which goes 'in' PE.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to stall deliberately so as to gain time.

clue.text: Article attracted prince

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
drew, as in drew a crowd, means attracted

explanation.surface: A newspaper feature caught the eye of a royal.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Andrew is a son of Queen Elizabeth II, so the name fits a prince.

clue.text: Language used in spacecraft on gantry

indicators.note: used in says the answer sits inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A space mission's crew speak a particular tongue on the launch gantry.
explanation.definitionFit: The language of Tonga, a Pacific island kingdom, is called by this name.

clue.text: Cattle without water

definitions.meaning: an old word for oxen and cows
a drink served with nothing added, undiluted

explanation.definitionFit: Neat is an archaic term for cattle, and a neat spirit is one taken undiluted.

clue.text: One employed to protect rhinos, say, prepared study about conflict

definitions.text: One employed to protect rhinos, say

parts.note: to be game is to be ready or willing
war is armed conflict
a den is a private room for study or work

explanation.surface: A conservation worker is described as someone ready to research warfare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is read in its sense of 'on the subject of': a study about conflict is a WAR DEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A game warden is employed to protect wildlife, rhinos being one example of game.

clue.text: Entertainer to steal article during part of play

indicators.note: during puts the stealing and the article within the part of the play

parts.note: an act is a main division of a play
to rob is to steal
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A performer steals something in the middle of a stage performance.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrobat is a performer of gymnastic feats, a circus entertainer.

clue.text: Bureaucrat in bar started to lose heart earlier

indicators.note: earlier means this piece comes first, before the next
losing its heart means the middle letter of the synonym goes

parts.note: began means started
a counter is the bar of a shop or pub

explanation.surface: A civil servant in a pub had already become disheartened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lose heart' means the middle letter goes; 'earlier' sets that shortened word in front. A bean counter is a mildly mocking term.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal term is for an accountant or official obsessed with costs and figures.

clue.text: Fabric brought out of Welsh river with corroded backing

parts.note: the Taff is the river that flows through Cardiff

indicators.note: backing means the word is read backwards

parts.note: rust ate the metal, it corroded it

explanation.surface: A cloth is fished out of a river in Wales with rust on its back.
explanation.definitionFit: Taffeta is a crisp, lustrous woven silk or synthetic cloth.

clue.text: Elected oddball, dressed for the part

parts.note: a party voted in is elected
a character is an eccentric person

explanation.surface: An eccentric newly voted in turns up in costume.
explanation.definitionFit: An actor in character is in the role, as if costumed and playing the part.

clue.text: Briefly lost Asian ruler in Russian city

indicators.note: briefly means the synonym is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: astray means lost, off the right path
a khan was a ruler in Central Asia, as Genghis Khan

explanation.surface: A Central Asian monarch has gone missing for a while in a city in Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: Astrakhan is a city in southern Russia on the Volga delta.

clue.text: Flag sellers?

parts.note: a flag is also the iris plant, so its sellers are people in the flower trade

explanation.definitionFit: Florists sell flowers, and the yellow flag is a kind of iris.

clue.text: Cancel immediately, say

indicators.note: say signals that the words are spoken aloud and matched by sound

parts.note: right off means at once, immediately

explanation.surface: Someone is told to call something off at once.
explanation.definitionFit: To write off a debt is to cancel it as never to be paid.

clue.text: Supporter comes after to provide food (grub)

indicators.note: the supporting piece comes after the other one

parts.note: to cater is to provide food
a pillar is a column that supports a building

explanation.surface: A backer arrives later to serve the meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grub' looks like slang for food, matching the surface, but it is a larva.
explanation.definitionFit: A grub is an insect larva, and a caterpillar is the larva of a butterfly or moth.

clue.text: Braved unexpectedly and unwisely, for example

indicators.note: something done unexpectedly comes out of its usual order, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Someone acted bravely, out of the blue and rather foolishly.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwisely is a word modifying a verb, an example of that part of speech.

clue.text: Spoil copper's boy

parts.note: to mar is to spoil
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, and the 's adds an S

explanation.surface: A policeman's son is being spoilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' looks like a police officer but is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcus is a boy's given name.

clue.text: Count gold eccentric, about 50, brought over

indicators.note: brought over means the whole run is turned round
about means the gold goes around the number

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
a card is an eccentric or amusing person

explanation.surface: An odd nobleman of about fifty is brought over with his gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Count' looks like a verb but is the title of a nobleman; 'brought over' turns the whole run ALUCARD around.
explanation.definitionFit: Dracula is the vampire count of Bram Stoker's novel.

clue.text: Clown to run backwards on jetty

indicators.note: on means this piece is added onto the end of the other

parts.note: a pier is a jetty

indicators.note: backwards means the two pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for run in cricket scoring

explanation.surface: A clown is told to run in reverse along a jetty.
explanation.definitionFit: Pierrot is the sad white-faced clown of French pantomime.

clue.text: Examine dressing gown straight after end of sleep

indicators.note: straight after means the gown comes immediately after that letter
end of picks out the last letter of the word

parts.note: a robe is a dressing gown

explanation.surface: Someone inspects their dressing gown on waking.
explanation.definitionFit: To probe is to investigate or examine closely.

clue.text: Family shield chosen — cute, when redesigned

indicators.note: redesigned means remade in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A family's coat of arms was selected because it was pretty once revamped.
explanation.definitionFit: An escutcheon is the shield on which a coat of arms is displayed.

clue.text: Endless industrial action in Scandinavian port

indicators.note: endless means both the first and last letters are cut off

parts.note: a go-slow is a form of industrial action by workers

explanation.surface: A dockers' dispute drags on without end in a Nordic harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' strips G and W from GOSLOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Oslo is the capital of Norway and a major seaport.

clue.text: Former US president meeting forest officer, backwoodsman

parts.note: Bush is the surname of two former US presidents
a ranger patrols and looks after a forest

explanation.surface: An ex-president meets a forest warden.
explanation.definitionFit: A bushranger was an outlaw living in the Australian bush, someone of the backwoods.

clue.text: Some fellas I fancy? I very much doubt it!

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone scoffs at the idea that any of the men they like would be interested.
explanation.definitionFit: The scornful retort expresses disbelief that something will ever happen.
